title: marrubium parviflorum subsp. oligodon
intro: Marrubium parviflorum subsp. oligodon, commonly known as a subspecies of the horehound plant, is a perennial herb in the mint family. It is valued for its medicinal properties, which include treating digestive issues, such as indigestion and diarrhea, thanks to its anti-inflammatory and antispasmodic effects. The bioactive constituents of Marrubium parviflorum subsp. oligodon include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and diterpenes, which contribute to its therapeutic actions, including antimicrobial and antioxidant activities. Additionally, the plant has been traditionally used to relieve respiratory issues, such as coughs and colds, due to its expectorant properties.
